newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Beach Pete farms in to Timor Sea permit.
newsitem.headline: Beach Pete farms in to Timor Sea permit.

text.p: Beach Petroleum NL said it had agreed in principle to farm in to Timor Sea exploration permit WA-199-P to earn a 10 percent interest.
Under the proposed agreement, Beach would earn its interest in exchange for contributing to the Kittiwake-1 exploration well which is scheduled for drilling in November this year, it said.
The stakes of participants in the WA-199-P joint venture will then be Boral Ltd's Boral Energy Ltd (operator) 36.31 percent, Santos Ltd 40.85 percent, Petroz NL 12.84 percent and Beach 10 percent.
The permit is located on the Londonderry High to the west of permit WA-260-P which was awarded to The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd in 1995 for an 11-well commitment, Beach said.
Four wells have been drilled in WA-260-P so far, three of which have been significant oil discoveries, it said.
The Kittiwake Prospect is situated in the northern corner of WA-199-P, about 250 km offshore and in less than 100 metres of water.
The structure is a tilted fault block with an east-west trend, similar to the adjacent oil discoveries of Laminaria, Buller, Elang, Buffalo and Kakatua, Beach said.

As in the adjacent oilfields, the primary target of Kittiwake-1 is the sandstone reservoirs of the Montara/Plover formations, expected at 2700 metres sub-sea, with the hydrocarbons being sourced from the Nancar Trough and/or the Sahul Syncline, Beach said.
Estimates of the reserves indicate a mean of 30 million barrels with a high side of 60 million barrels, it said.
